Prompt题目 1 Talking at work职场沟通

Talk about a time when you were late for something important. 说一次重要的事你迟到了。

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. Set the scene: an important appointment背景：一个重要的约定
  2. Why you were late: a bus problem迟到的原因：公交出了问题
  3. How it ended and what you learned结果和教训

  • a review /ə rɪˈvjuː/ 评论；书评；影评；乐评
    Since then I have never gone into a review without a list. What I Have Learned from Ten Performance Reviews
  • figure out /ˌfɪɡər ˈaʊt/ 弄明白；想出办法
    Use the empty hours to figure out who does what. The First Week: What Nobody Tells You
  • follow up /ˌfɒləʊ ˈʌp/ 跟进

Three sample answers on the same plan同一骨架的三级示范

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 72 words词

A few months ago, I had a job interview at nine o'clock. I got up at seven.

But the bus didn't come. I waited for twenty minutes. Then I took a taxi, but there was a lot of traffic. I was fifteen minutes late.

I was very embarrassed. I said sorry to the manager. She was nice, and the interview was OK.

Now I always leave one hour early for important things.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Countable and uncountable nounsEvery clause needs a subjectGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedhave: main verb, auxiliary and fixed phrases

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 116 words词

A few months ago, I had a job interview downtown at nine o'clock. I got up at seven, and I thought I had lots of time.

But when I got to the bus stop, the bus didn't come. I waited for twenty minutes, and I started to panic. Finally, I took a taxi, but there was a lot of traffic. I arrived fifteen minutes late.

I was so embarrassed. I said sorry to the manager and explained what happened. Luckily, she was very kind and the interview went well.

After that day, I learned an important lesson. Now I always leave one hour early for important things, and I check the bus schedule the night before.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Countable and uncountable nounsPast simple and past continuous in storiesGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedhave: main verb, auxiliary and fixed phrasesEveryday verbs beyond get and goCompound nouns and compound adjectives

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 127 words词

A few months ago, I had a job interview downtown at nine, and I left home at seven, thinking I had plenty of time to spare.

Then everything went wrong. The bus simply never showed up, and after twenty minutes of pacing at the stop, I started to panic. I eventually flagged down a taxi, only to get stuck in rush-hour traffic, and I rushed in a good fifteen minutes late.

I was absolutely mortified. I apologized to the manager and briefly explained what had happened. Fortunately, she was very understanding, and the interview actually went well.

That morning taught me a lesson I've never forgotten. These days, I leave a full hour early for anything important, and I always check the bus schedule the night before.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Countable and uncountable nounsVerb and noun endings you cannot skipGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedNarrative tenses and the past perfectPrepositions after verbs, and no preposition at allhave: main verb, auxiliary and fixed phrasesReduced relative clausesEveryday verbs beyond get and goChinglish and false friends

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I got up at seven. → I got up at seven, and I thought I had lots of time. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Adding what you thought at the time (lots of time) sets up the problem, so the story has a turn.加上当时的想法（以为时间很多），为后面的「出事」做铺垫，故事有起伏。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I waited for twenty minutes. → I waited for twenty minutes, and I started to panic. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Adding the feeling lets the listener share the tension.加上感受，听的人能跟着紧张起来。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I was so embarrassed. → I was absolutely mortified. Vocabulary词汇
    "Mortified" is more precise and stronger than "so embarrassed".mortified（羞愧极了）比 so embarrassed 更精准、更有分量。
  • 7–8 → 9+ Finally, I took a taxi, but there was a lot of traffic. → I eventually flagged down a taxi, only to get stuck in rush-hour traffic Listenability好懂程度
    "Only to ..." shows a disappointing result: an advanced pattern for a twist in a story.only to … 表示「结果却……」，是讲故事时制造反转的高级句型。
  • 7–8 → 9+ After that day, I learned an important lesson. → That morning taught me a lesson I've never forgotten. Listenability好懂程度
    Making "that morning" the subject varies the sentence and is stronger than "I learned a lesson".让 that morning 做主语，句式有变化，也比 learned a lesson 更有力。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • First give the time, place and how important the event was, so the listener knows why being "late" was a problem.先交代时间、地点、事情有多重要，让听的人知道「迟到」为什么是个问题。
  • It is all in the past tense (got up, waited, arrived) and the order is clear. The single word "Luckily" brings in the turn.全程过去时（got up, waited, arrived），顺序清楚；Luckily 一个词就带出转折。
  • Common mistake: mixing up "late" and "delay". To say "I was late", use "I was late", not "I delayed".常见错误：把 late 和 delay 混用；说「我迟到了」用 I was late，不要说 I delayed。

Three sample answers on the same plan同一骨架的三级示范

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 68 words词

Last winter, my family had dinner at my sister's house. It was my mother's birthday. My sister cooked a lot of food.

We ate dumplings, fish and a big chocolate cake. My little nephew sang happy birthday very loud, and everyone laughed.

After dinner, my mother told stories. Nobody wanted to go home.

I remember this dinner because the food was very good and my family was together.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Verb + -ing or to: the common verbsEvery clause needs a subjectCompound nouns and possessives: a car key, the car's ownerGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedhave: main verb, auxiliary and fixed phrasesLinkers without doubling

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 114 words词

Last winter, my whole family had dinner at my sister's house in Burnaby. It was my mother's sixty-fifth birthday, and my sister cooked for two days.

When I walked in, the house smelled amazing. We sat around a big table and ate dumplings, fish and a huge chocolate cake. My little nephew sang happy birthday very loudly and very badly, and everyone was laughing.

After dinner, my mother told stories about her childhood, and we listened for a long time. Nobody wanted to go home.

I still remember that night, because the food was delicious, but more importantly, the whole family was together. It was warm and happy, even though it was snowing outside.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Verb + -ing or to: the common verbsPast simple and past continuous in storiesEvery clause needs a subjectCompound nouns and possessives: a car key, the car's ownerhave: main verb, auxiliary and fixed phrasesBeyond very good: stronger adjectivesLinkers without doublingNumbers, dates, prices and quantitiesThe senses and the body: how things look, sound and feel

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 127 words词

Last winter, my whole family gathered at my sister's place in Burnaby for my mother's sixty-fifth birthday. My sister had spent two full days cooking.

The moment I walked in, the house smelled incredible. We squeezed around one big table and feasted on dumplings, steamed fish and an enormous chocolate cake. My little nephew belted out happy birthday, loudly and hilariously off-key, and the whole table burst out laughing.

Afterwards, my mother told stories from her childhood that even I had never heard. Nobody wanted the evening to end.

What makes that night stick in my memory isn't just the food, delicious as it was. It's that, for once, all of us were in one room. It felt so warm, even with the snow coming down outside.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Giving reasons: as, since, due to, withCompound nouns and possessives: a car key, the car's ownerNarrative tenses and the past perfectQuantifiers: all, most, each, every, eitherRelative clauses with prepositions and quantifiersVerb + object + infinitiveBeyond very good: stronger adjectivesNumbers, dates, prices and quantitiesPrepositions of time and place that differ from ChineseNear-synonyms: say, tell, speak, talk and othersThe senses and the body: how things look, sound and feel

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 My sister cooked a lot of food. → my sister cooked for two days Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "Cooked for two days" is a concrete detail; the listener can picture it better than "a lot of food".「做了两天」是具体细节，比 a lot of food 更能让人想象。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 the food was very good and my family was together → the food was delicious, but more importantly, the whole family was together Listenability好懂程度
    "More importantly" ranks the two reasons, so the ending has depth.more importantly 把两个理由分出轻重，结尾更有层次。
  • 7–8 → 9+ ate dumplings, fish and a huge chocolate cake → feasted on dumplings, steamed fish and an enormous chocolate cake Vocabulary词汇
    "Feasted on", "steamed" and "enormous" make the picture richer.feast on（大吃一顿）、steamed、enormous 让画面更丰富。
  • 7–8 → 9+ sang happy birthday very loudly and very badly → belted out happy birthday, loudly and hilariously off-key Vocabulary词汇
    "Belted out" and "off-key" are precise words for singing.belt out（放声唱）、off-key（跑调）是精准的场景词。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I still remember that night, because the food was delicious → What makes that night stick in my memory isn't just the food, delicious as it was. Listenability好懂程度
    A "what" clause as subject plus the concessive "delicious as it was": complex structures of Level 9 and above.what 引导的主语从句加 delicious as it was 的让步倒装，是 9 级以上的复杂句型。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • First say who, where and what occasion, then the food and atmosphere, and finally say "why it was memorable". These three steps match the question exactly.先说谁、哪里、什么场合，再说食物和气氛，最后点明「为什么难忘」，三步正好对应题目。
  • Sensory details (it smelled great, he sang loudly and badly) give the story a picture.感官细节（闻起来很香、唱得很大声也很难听）让故事有画面。
  • Common mistake: only listing food names. The story is about people and feelings. The food is just background.常见错误：只列食物名字。故事重点是人和感受，食物只是背景。

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 71 words词

I remember my first day at my new job. I was very nervous.

When I arrived, I couldn't find the office. A woman helped me. Her name was Linda. She is my friend now.

The first hours were hard. I forgot my password. I didn't know the printer. But people helped me, and my manager took me to lunch.

At the end of the day, I felt better. I was happy.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Past simple and past continuous in storiesArticles: a, the or nothingGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhausted

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 119 words词

I remember my first day at my new job in Richmond. I was very nervous that morning, and I changed my clothes three times.

When I arrived, I couldn't find the office, and I walked around the building twice. A woman saw me and asked, "Are you lost?" Her name was Linda, and she took me to my desk. She became my friend.

The first hours were hard. I forgot my password, and I didn't know how to use the printer. But everyone was helpful, and my manager took me to lunch.

By the end of the day, I felt much better. It wasn't as bad as I thought, and I was excited to come back the next day.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Past simple and past continuous in storiesArticles: a, the or nothing

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 130 words词

I'll never forget my first day at my new job in Richmond. I was so jittery that morning that I changed my outfit three times.

To make matters worse, I couldn't find the office and ended up circling the building twice. A woman noticed me wandering and asked, "Are you lost?" That was Linda, who walked me to my desk and later became one of my closest friends.

The first few hours were a blur. I forgot my password and couldn't figure out the printer, but my colleagues were incredibly patient, and my manager even took me out for lunch.

By the end of the day, the knot in my stomach was gone. It was nowhere near as bad as I'd imagined, and I actually couldn't wait to go back.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Countable and uncountable nounsEvery clause needs a subjectArticles: a, the or nothingFuture forms: will, going to, present tensesGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedDefining and non-defining relative clausesEveryday verbs beyond get and goChinglish and false friendsPhrasal verbs for work

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 A woman helped me. → A woman saw me and asked, "Are you lost?" Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    A line of real dialogue instead of a summary brings the story to life.用一句对话代替概括，故事一下子活了。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 At the end of the day, I felt better. I was happy. → By the end of the day, I felt much better. It wasn't as bad as I thought Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Contrasting with the morning nerves (not as bad as I thought) gives the ending a change.和早上的紧张做对比（没想象中那么糟），结尾有变化。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I was very nervous that morning, and I changed my clothes three times. → I was so jittery that morning that I changed my outfit three times. Listenability好懂程度
    "So ... that" puts cause and result in one sentence, and "jittery" is livelier than "nervous".so … that 结构把原因和结果放进一句，jittery 也比 nervous 生动。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I couldn't find the office, and I walked around the building twice → To make matters worse, I couldn't find the office and ended up circling the building twice. Listenability好懂程度
    "To make matters worse" is a storytelling linker, and "ended up" shows the unplanned result.to make matters worse 是讲故事的衔接语；ended up 表示「结果却」。
  • 7–8 → 9+ By the end of the day, I felt much better. → By the end of the day, the knot in my stomach was gone. Vocabulary词汇
    "The knot in my stomach" is a vivid image of nerves.the knot in my stomach（胃里打结＝紧张）是形象的比喻。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • "Nervous, then meeting someone, then mistakes also helped, then a relaxed ending" is the safest structure for a first-day story.「紧张 → 遇到人 → 出错也有帮助 → 结尾轻松」是第一天故事最稳的结构。
  • Small details like "changed my clothes three times" sound more like a real person than "I felt very nervous".changed my clothes three times 这类小细节，比 I felt very nervous 更像真人。
  • Common mistake: saying "the first time day" for "first day". Use "my first day at ...".常见错误：把 first day 说成 the first time day。用 my first day at …。

Prompt题目 4 Finding a home找房与安家

Talk about a time when something broke at home and you had to fix it. 说家里东西坏了你得修的一次。

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点

Chunks from the same topic you could use可以用上的同主题词块
  • since /sɪns/ 自从（表示时间起点）
    I have told this story to every newcomer I have met since. Twelve Viewings and One Lesson
  • look /lʊk/ 看起来，显得

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 131 words词

Last spring, the kitchen sink in my apartment sprang a leak. I came out one morning to find a puddle spreading across the floor, and my heart dropped.

My first move was to call the landlord, but he didn't pick up. Rather than sit around waiting, I looked it up online and found a step-by-step video on replacing the pipe under the sink. I headed to the hardware store and picked up the part for just ten dollars.

The job took about an hour, and I got thoroughly soaked in the process. But when I finally turned on the tap, not a single drop came out.

I was genuinely proud of myself. A plumber would have charged around two hundred dollars, and these days small repairs don't intimidate me at all.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 So I watched a video online. → I didn't want to wait, so I searched online and found a video. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Saying why you didn't wait gives the action a reason.先说为什么不等（不想等），行动就有了理由。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 A plumber is very expensive, so I saved money. → A plumber would have cost me about two hundred dollars Listenability好懂程度
    "Would have cost" is a conditional, and the exact amount is more convincing than "very expensive".would have cost 是虚拟语气，再加具体金额，比 very expensive 更有说服力。
  • 7–8 → 9+ started leaking → sprang a leak Vocabulary词汇
    "Spring a leak" is the set expression for starting to leak.spring a leak 是「开始漏水」的固定搭配。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I didn't want to wait, so I searched online and found a video. → Rather than sit around waiting, I looked it up online Listenability好懂程度
    Opening with "rather than" varies the sentence pattern.rather than 开头的结构变化了句式。
  • 7–8 → 9+ But when I turned on the tap, nothing leaked! → not a single drop came out Vocabulary词汇
    "Not a single drop" is an emphatic negative that is more vivid than "nothing leaked".not a single drop 用否定强调，比 nothing leaked 更有画面感。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • Numbers (ten dollars, one hour, two hundred dollars) make the story specific, and give you something to say when you are nervous.数字（十块、一小时、两百块）让故事具体，也方便你在紧张时有话可说。
  • "But when I turned on the tap, nothing leaked!" is the turning point of the story. Say it with stress.But when I turned on the tap, nothing leaked! 这一句是故事的转折，用重音读出来。
  • Common mistake: mixing up "pipe" and "tap". If you're not sure, say "the thing under the sink" and don't pause too long.常见错误：pipe 和 tap 记混。不确定就说 the thing under the sink，不要停顿太久。

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 126 words词

Two summers ago, my husband and I planned a three-day getaway to Tofino. We were dying to see the open Pacific and just unwind.

But halfway there, the car broke down near Nanaimo in the blazing heat. We had to call a tow truck, and the mechanic told us the repair would take at least two days.

So, rather than let it ruin our holiday, we made the best of it. We checked into a small hotel in Nanaimo, wandered along the beach and treated ourselves to fish and chips by the water. We never did make it to Tofino.

Funnily enough, it turned out to be one of our favourite trips. It reminded us that where you go matters far less than who you're with.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 We wanted to see the ocean. → We wanted to see the ocean and relax for three days. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    One more detail (three days to relax) makes the plan concrete and the later change sharper.多一个细节（放松三天），计划更具体，后面的「没去成」也更有对比。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 But it was a good trip. → In the end, it was a great trip anyway. Listenability好懂程度
    "In the end" and "anyway" mark a surprising outcome.in the end、anyway 两个衔接词标出「结局出乎意料」。
  • 7–8 → 9+ So we changed our plans. → rather than let it ruin our holiday, we made the best of it Vocabulary词汇
    "Make the best of it" is the natural idiom for coping well.make the best of it（随遇而安、尽量往好处做）是地道的固定说法。
  • 7–8 → 9+ We never got to Tofino. → We never did make it to Tofino. Listenability好懂程度
    The emphatic "did" and "make it to" carry a note of regret.did 加强语气，make it to 是「到达」的口语说法，读起来有遗憾的味道。
  • 7–8 → 9+ the best part of a trip is not the place. It's the time together → where you go matters far less than who you're with Listenability好懂程度
    Two noun clauses in contrast (where you go, who you're with) make a crisp ending.两个名词从句对比（去哪里 vs 和谁），结尾简洁有力。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • "Plan, then a problem, then a changed plan, then it turned out fine" is an all-purpose structure for this kind of question.「计划 → 出问题 → 改计划 → 反而不错」是这类题的万能结构。
  • "We changed our plans" is very useful. You can use it in almost any story about something going wrong.we changed our plans 很实用，几乎任何「出问题」的故事都可以套。
  • Common mistake: saying "broken" instead of "broke down". For a car that stopped, use "broke down" or "stopped working".常见错误：把 broke down 说成 broken。车坏了用 broke down 或 stopped working。

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 122 words词

Last year, I decided to learn how to swim. I grew up far from the ocean, and I never learned. But my kids love the pool, and I wanted to join them.

I signed up for a class at the community centre. At first, it was harder than I thought. I was afraid of putting my face in the water, and I almost gave up after the first lesson.

But my teacher was patient. She told me to practise a little every week. Little by little, I got better, and after two months, I could swim across the pool.

Now I swim with my children every Sunday. I feel proud, and I learned that it's never too late to learn something new.

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 136 words词

Last year, I finally decided to learn how to swim. I grew up far from the ocean and never had the chance, but my kids adore the pool, and I was tired of watching from the side.

I enrolled in a beginners' class at the community centre, and honestly, it was far tougher than I'd expected. I was terrified of putting my face underwater, and after the first lesson I came close to quitting.

Luckily, my instructor was incredibly patient. She encouraged me to practise a little every week, and gradually it started to click. Within two months, I could swim the full length of the pool.

These days I swim with my children every Sunday. Not only am I proud of myself, but I've also learned it's never too late to pick up something new.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 But my kids love the pool. → But my kids love the pool, and I wanted to join them. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Stating the real motive (to join the kids) completes the reason.说出真正的动机（想和孩子一起游），学游泳的理由更完整。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was afraid of the water. → I was afraid of putting my face in the water, and I almost gave up Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "Afraid of putting my face in the water" is more specific, and "almost gave up" adds drama.「怕把脸放进水里」比「怕水」具体，almost gave up 制造了起伏。
  • 7–8 → 9+ At first, it was harder than I thought. → it was far tougher than I'd expected Listenability好懂程度
    "Far" strengthens the comparison, and the past perfect "I'd expected" gets the time right.far 强化比较级，I'd expected 用过去完成时，时间关系更准确。
  • 7–8 → 9+ Little by little, I got better → gradually it started to click Vocabulary词汇
    "It started to click" is the natural spoken way to say something finally made sense.it started to click（开窍了）是口语里形容「突然会了」的地道说法。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I feel proud, and I learned that it's never too late → Not only am I proud of myself, but I've also learned it's never too late Listenability好懂程度
    "Not only ... but also" with inversion is the kind of complex grammar the Level 9 description mentions.not only … but also 加倒装，是官方 9 级描述里的「复杂句型」。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • First say why you learned (to play with my child). A motive gives the story a human touch.先说为什么学（想和孩子一起玩），动机让故事有人情味。
  • "I almost gave up" is natural spoken English that shows how hard it really felt.I almost gave up 是很自然的口语，表示困难时的真实感受。
  • Common mistake: saying "I learned swimming". To say you learned to swim, say "I learned how to swim".常见错误：说 I learned swimming。学会游泳说 I learned how to swim。

A few months ago, I struck up a conversation with a fascinating man on the SkyTrain. I was heading home after work, and he was sitting beside me cradling a small, well-worn guitar.

We got talking about music. It turned out he was seventy and had emigrated from Italy fifty years earlier. He'd spent his whole career on a factory floor, yet every single weekend he played in the park, purely for the joy of it.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 He had a small guitar. → he was sitting next to me with a small guitar Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Placing the man in the scene (sitting next to me) helps the listener picture it.把人放进画面（坐在我旁边），听的人更容易想象。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 He never took a lesson. He just loved music. → I was surprised to learn that he never took a lesson. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Adding your own reaction (surprised) gives the experience feeling.加上自己的反应（很惊讶），经历就有了感情。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I met an interesting man on the SkyTrain → I struck up a conversation with a fascinating man on the SkyTrain Vocabulary词汇
    "Struck up a conversation" and "fascinating" are more precise than "met" and "interesting".strike up a conversation（搭上话）、fascinating 比 met、interesting 更精确。
  • 7–8 → 9+ He worked in a factory all his life, but every weekend, he played music in the park for free. → He'd spent his whole career on a factory floor, yet every single weekend he played in the park, purely for the joy of it. Listenability好懂程度
    "Yet" makes the contrast, and "purely for the joy of it" names the motive, giving the sentence rhythm.yet 做转折，purely for the joy of it 点出动机，句子更有节奏。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I was surprised to learn that he never took a lesson. → What struck me most was that he'd never had a single lesson Listenability好懂程度
    "What struck me most" is a subject clause that puts the focus on the surprise.what struck me most 是主语从句，把重点放在最惊讶的地方。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • The people in the story need one or two specific facts (seventy years old, came from Italy, plays piano in the park on weekends), without complex words.故事里的人物要有一两个具体的信息（七十岁、从意大利来、周末公园弹琴），不用复杂词。
  • Direct speech (he said, "...") gives the story a voice and is easy to read naturally.直接引语（he said, "…"）让故事有声音，也容易读得自然。
  • Common mistake: "he said me". The correct forms are "he said to me" or "he told me".常见错误：he said me。正确是 he said to me 或 he told me。

  • left behind /left bɪˈhaɪnd/ 被落下的

Last year, my best friend gave me a small notebook for my birthday. On the surface, it was nothing fancy, just plain blue with my name on the cover.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was new in Canada, and I was lonely. → She knew that I was new in Canada and often felt lonely. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Telling it from what she knew shows the thought behind the gift.从「她知道」的角度讲，礼物的用心就出来了。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 It was not expensive, but it was special. → It was special because she remembered how I felt. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "Because" explains why it was special instead of only saying so.用 because 说出为什么特别，而不是只下结论。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I didn't expect that, and I almost cried. → It caught me completely off guard, and I had to fight back tears. Vocabulary词汇
    "Caught me off guard" and "fight back tears" are idiomatic expressions.catch someone off guard（措手不及）、fight back tears（忍住眼泪）都是地道表达。
  • 7–8 → 9+ It wasn't expensive, but she put her time and her heart into it. → What made it so meaningful wasn't the price tag; it was the thought behind it. Listenability好懂程度
    A "what" clause and a semicolon contrast state the gift's real value.what 主语从句加分号对比，说出了礼物的真正价值。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I read the old pages, and I feel better → it never fails to lift my spirits Vocabulary词汇
    "Never fails to" and "lift my spirits" say more than "feel better".never fails to、lift my spirits（让我振作）比 feel better 有层次。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • It doesn't matter if the gift itself is ordinary. What matters is "why it was special". This answer talks about the friend's thoughtfulness.礼物本身普通没关系，重点是「为什么特别」，答案里讲的是朋友的用心。
  • A concession like "It wasn't expensive, but ..." is very useful for saying "not expensive but meaningful".It wasn't expensive, but … 这种让步句型很好用，表达「不贵但有意义」。
  • Common mistake: using "receive" and "get" interchangeably. In speech, "got a gift" is more natural.常见错误：receive 和 get 随便混用。口语里 got a gift 更自然。

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 Then my computer stopped. → Then my computer stopped working, and two customers were waiting for me on the phone. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Stacking the pressures (computer down plus customers waiting) shows how hard the day was.压力叠加（电脑坏了＋客户在等），故事的「难」才说清楚。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was very tired, but I was happy. → I was exhausted, but I felt relieved. Vocabulary词汇
    "Exhausted" and "relieved" are more accurate than "very tired" and "happy".exhausted、relieved 比 very tired、happy 更准确。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I had the most stressful day at work → I had what was probably the most stressful day of my working life Listenability好懂程度
    The "what" clause plus "probably" sounds natural without overstating.what 从句加 probably，语气更自然，也不夸张。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I felt like crying. → For a moment I felt completely overwhelmed. Vocabulary词汇
    "Overwhelmed" is the precise word for stress like this.overwhelmed（应接不暇、崩溃）是描写压力的精准词。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I sent the report ten minutes before five → submitted the report with ten minutes to spare Vocabulary词汇
    "With ten minutes to spare" is the natural collocation.with … to spare（还剩……）是地道搭配。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • Structure for a stress story: problems pile up (report, computer, phone), then my response, then the result.压力故事的结构：问题叠加（报告、电脑、电话）→ 我的应对 → 结果。
  • An action like "Took a deep breath and made a list" shows how you handled the problem better than "I was very stressed".Took a deep breath and made a list 这种应对动作比 I was very stressed 更能说明你怎样处理问题。
  • Common mistake: mixing up "stressful" and "stressed". The situation is stressful; the person is stressed.常见错误：stressful 和 stressed 混用。事情是 stressful，人是 stressed。

The moment I spotted it, my heart sank. Instead of hoping no one would notice, I went straight to my boss, then called the client to explain, asked him to delete the email and sent the correct version.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 When I saw it, I was scared. → When I saw it, my heart sank. Vocabulary词汇
    "My heart sank" is the idiomatic way to react to bad news.my heart sank（心一沉）是描写坏消息的地道说法。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 My boss was not angry. She said mistakes happen. → she was glad I told her quickly Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Adding why the boss wasn't angry (I told her quickly) makes the ending make sense.加上老板为什么不生气（我很快就说了），结局更有道理。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I told my boss right away → Instead of hoping no one would notice, I went straight to my boss Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Naming the other option (hoping no one notices) before your action shows judgment.说出另一个选择（侥幸不说）再说自己怎么做，显出判断力。
  • 7–8 → 9+ My boss wasn't angry. → To my relief, my boss wasn't upset at all. Listenability好懂程度
    Opening with "to my relief" puts feeling and fact in one sentence.to my relief 开头，把情绪和事实放在一句里。
  • 7–8 → 9+ it saves a lot of trouble → saves a world of trouble Vocabulary词汇
    "A world of trouble" is a lively spoken intensifier.a world of（大量的）是生动的口语强调。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • "Admit the mistake and fix it right away" shows better character than "I made no mistakes". Raters care that you tell it clearly.「承认错误、马上补救」比「没犯错」更能体现好品质，评分员看重的是你讲得清楚。
  • "My heart sank" is a common spoken phrase and not too hard. If you'd rather not use it, "I felt terrible" is perfectly fine.my heart sank 是常见口语，不会太难；若不想用，说 I felt terrible 也完全可以。
  • Common mistake: mixing up "mistake" and "error". In speech, "mistake" is enough.常见错误：mistake 和 error 混用，口语里说 mistake 就行。

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I didn't open it for a week, because I thought it was not important. → I left the envelope on the table for a week Vocabulary词汇
    "Left the envelope on the table" is a picture the listener can see, more real than "didn't open it".left the envelope on the table 是一个看得见的画面，比 didn't open it 更像真事。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was very surprised → my heart sank Vocabulary词汇
    "My heart sank" is the natural phrase for bad news, and more accurate than "very surprised".my heart sank 是讲坏消息时的地道说法，比 very surprised 准确：不是惊讶，是心一沉。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 gave them my number → I gave them the reference number at the top of the letter Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "Reference number" is a chunk from this topic; saying where it is on the letter makes the detail concrete.reference number 是本主题文章的词块；说清是信上方的参考编号，细节就具体了。
  • 7–8 → 9+ When I finally opened it → When I finally got round to opening it Vocabulary词汇
    "Get round to doing" means finally doing something you kept putting off, which echoes the week of delay.get round to doing 表示「拖了很久才去做」，正好呼应前面放了一周。
  • 7–8 → 9+ and asked for an extension → politely asked whether an extension was possible Task Fulfillment完成任务
    The indirect question "whether ... was possible" is more polite and shows how you spoke.间接问句 whether … was possible 更客气，讲出了自己当时的语气。
  • 7–8 → 9+ Since then, I open every official letter the same day. → The lesson stuck Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "The lesson stuck" signals the change before the new habit, so the ending lands harder.The lesson stuck 先点出「这件事改变了我」，再说现在的习惯，结尾更有分量。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • The story runs delay, problem, fix, lesson: four short parts that fit 60 seconds.故事按「拖延→发现问题→解决→教训」走，60 秒正好四小段。
  • Reference number, late fee and extension are chunks from this topic; a detail like quoting the reference number sounds more real than "I called".reference number、late fee、extension 都是本主题文章里的词块；说清「报了参考编号」这种细节，比「我打了电话」更像真事。
  • One line of lesson at the end (the same day) gives Task 2 the "what it meant to you" part.结尾一句教训（the same day）收口，Task 2 要的「这件事对你意味着什么」就有了。

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 79 words词

Two years ago my father fell in the kitchen. He was not badly hurt, but he was scared.

The doctor said he needed to make his legs stronger. So he started a class at the community centre, two times a week. At first it was hard, and his legs hurt. He wanted to stop.

But he did not stop. After three months he could stand up from a chair easily. Now he walks every day, and he is happier.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Verb + -ing or to: the common verbsEvery clause needs a subjectVerb and noun endings you cannot skipQuantifiers: all, most, each, every, either

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 114 words词

Two years ago my father slipped in the kitchen. He wasn't badly hurt, but it really scared him, and it was a wake-up call for our whole family.

His doctor told him that after sixty, muscle strength drops quickly, so he suggested a strength and balance class. My dad joined one at the community centre, twice a week. The first month was tough. His knees were sore, and he wanted to quit.

But he kept it up. After about three months, he could get up from a low chair without using his hands, and he was walking much more confidently. Honestly, he seemed younger. Now he even goes on his own, rain or shine.

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 128 words词

Two years ago my father slipped in the kitchen. He wasn't badly hurt, but it shook his confidence, and it was a wake-up call for all of us.

His doctor explained that strength tends to drop off sharply after sixty unless you actively build it up, so he recommended a strength and balance class. Dad signed up at the community centre, twice a week. The first month was a real struggle: his knees ached, and more than once he threatened to give up.

To his credit, he kept it up and paced himself. Within three months he could rise from a low chair without using his hands, and he carried himself with a confidence I hadn't seen in years. Watching him, I eventually started going along with him.

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 but he was scared → but it really scared him, and it was a wake-up call for our whole family Vocabulary词汇
    "Wake-up call" says what the fall meant: not just that he was scared, but that the whole family woke up.wake-up call（警钟）一下说出这件事的意义：不只他怕了，全家都醒了。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 The doctor said he needed to make his legs stronger. → muscle strength drops quickly Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Giving the doctor's reason (strength drops quickly after sixty) adds cause and effect to the story.说出医生给的理由（六十岁后肌肉力量下降快），故事就有了因果。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 But he did not stop. → But he kept it up. Vocabulary词汇
    "Keep it up" is a chunk from this topic meaning "keep going", more natural than "did not stop".keep it up 是本主题文章的词块，意思是「坚持下去」，比 did not stop 更地道。
  • 7–8 → 9+ muscle strength drops quickly → strength tends to drop off sharply after sixty unless you actively build it up Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Tend to, drop off and build up all come from this topic's texts; the "unless" clause states the condition: train or lose it.tend to、drop off、build up 都来自本主题文章；unless 从句把「不练就会掉」的条件说清了。
  • 7–8 → 9+ The first month was tough. → The first month was a real struggle Vocabulary词汇
    "A real struggle" followed by a colon and details paints a fuller picture than "tough".a real struggle 后面用冒号接具体细节，比 tough 更有画面。
  • 7–8 → 9+ Honestly, he seemed younger. → he carried himself with a confidence I hadn't seen in years Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    A visible change (how he carries himself) replaces the vague "seemed younger", so the ending lands.用一个看得见的变化（走路的样子）代替笼统的「显年轻」，结尾更有力。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • A personal story needs a turn: the fall (cause), the hard first month (struggle), the change after three months (result). It fits 60 seconds.经历题要有转折：摔跤（起因）→难坚持（困难）→三个月后的变化（结果），60 秒刚好讲完。
  • A detail you can picture (getting up from a low chair without using his hands) instead of "he got healthier" lifts the content score.用一个能看见的细节（不用手扶就能从矮椅子上站起来）代替「他身体好多了」，内容分就上去了。
  • Keep up, build up, pace yourself and community centre are all chunks from this topic's texts.keep up、build up、pace yourself、community centre 都是本主题文章里的词块。

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 74 words词

Last year I went to my son's school concert. He had a short song to sing alone.

Before his song, my phone made a sound. It was an email from work. I started to write an answer.

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 114 words词

Last spring I went to my son's school concert. He was nervous because he had a short solo, and he really wanted me to see it.

Just before his turn, my phone buzzed. It was an email from my manager, so I only glanced at it. But then I started typing a quick answer.

When I looked up, everyone was clapping. I had missed the whole thing, all forty seconds of it. After the show, my son asked, "Did you see me?" and I didn't know what to say. I felt terrible.

Since then, my phone stays in my pocket at family events, and I tell my manager I'm offline. The email could wait.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Past simple and past continuous in storiesEvery clause needs a subjectCompound nouns and possessives: a car key, the car's ownerNarrative tenses and the past perfectVerb + object + infinitivewhat, whatever, whoever as noun clausesLinkers without doublingPrepositions of time and place that differ from ChineseFeelings in fine grain

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 129 words词

Last spring I went to my son's school concert. He'd been practising a short solo for weeks, and he'd made me promise I'd be watching.

Just before his turn, my phone buzzed. It was my manager, and I told myself I'd only glance at it. Of course, a glance turned into a reply, and the reply turned into three.

By the time I looked up, the whole room was applauding. I'd missed it completely, all forty seconds of it. Afterwards he ran over, beaming, and asked, "Did you see me?" and I had no honest answer. I've rarely felt so small.

These days, without exception, my phone stays in my pocket at family events. Nothing at work has ever been that urgent, and I won't make that trade again.

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 He had a short song to sing alone. → he had a short solo Vocabulary词汇
    One word, "solo", replaces "a song to sing alone".solo 一个词替掉 a song to sing alone，更简洁。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I started to write an answer. → so I only glanced at it Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Saying you only meant to glance before you started typing creates the turn: you never planned to.先说「只是瞄一眼」再说「开始回」，才有「本来没打算」的转折。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I felt very bad. → I felt terrible. Vocabulary词汇
    "Terrible" is stronger and more natural in speech than "very bad".terrible 比 very bad 更强、更像口语。
  • 7–8 → 9+ But then I started typing a quick answer. → a glance turned into a reply, and the reply turned into three Listenability好懂程度
    "A glance turned into a reply, and the reply turned into three" shows attention being pulled away step by step.「一瞥变成一封、一封变成三封」的递进句，把注意力被一点点拖走讲得很生动。
  • 7–8 → 9+ everyone was clapping → the whole room was applauding Vocabulary词汇
    "The whole room" is more visual than "everyone".the whole room 比 everyone 更有画面感。
  • 7–8 → 9+ The email could wait. → Nothing at work has ever been that urgent Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    From "the email could wait" to "nothing at work has ever been that urgent": a deeper reflection.从「那封邮件可以等」上升到「工作上没有什么事值得这样」，反思更深。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • A personal story needs one concrete moment: the son asking "Did you see me?" carries the feeling without a string of "sad".经历题最好有一个具体时刻：儿子问「你看见我了吗？」，一句话就把感受讲出来，不必说很多 sad。
  • Glance at is a chunk from this topic; the 9+ answer uses "a glance turned into a reply, and the reply turned into three" to show attention being dragged away.glance at 是本主题文章的词块；9 级示范用「一瞥变成一封回复、一封变成三封」的递进句，把「注意力被拖走」讲得很生动。
  • Ending with what you do now gives the story meaning; Task 2 needs the lesson.结尾说现在怎么做，经历就有了意义，Task 2 的「学到什么」不能省。

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 75 words词

Last year my mother got a phone call. The man said he was from her bank. He knew her name.

He said someone was using her card, and she must move her money today. He wanted her password. My mother was scared.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Every clause needs a subjectGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedPrepositions of time and place that differ from Chinese

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 115 words词

Last year my mother got a call from a man who said he was from her bank. He knew her full name and the last four numbers of her card, so it sounded very real.

He told her someone was using her card overseas and she had to move her money right away. He kept saying it was urgent. My mother was scared, and she almost gave him her online banking code.

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 128 words词

Last year my mother got a call from someone claiming to be from her bank. He knew her full name and the last four digits of her card, which made the whole thing frighteningly convincing.

He told her a stranger was using her card overseas and that she had to move her savings immediately. He kept piling on the pressure, and she came within seconds of reading out her online banking code.

What saved her was a nagging feeling that something was off. She said she'd call back, hung up, and rang the number printed on her card. The bank confirmed it was a scam. Since then, our family has one simple rule: if in doubt, hang up and call back yourself, using a number you already trust.

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 He knew her name. → He knew her full name and the last four numbers of her card, so it sounded very real. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Saying how much the caller knew explains why she nearly believed him.说清骗子知道多少，才解释得了「为什么差点信了」。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 and ended the call → hung up Vocabulary词汇
    "Hang up" is a chunk from this topic and far more common in speech than "end the call".hang up（挂电话）是本主题文章的词块，口语里比 end the call 常用得多。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 My mother was scared. → she almost gave him her online banking code Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Adding that she almost gave the code creates the tension.加上「差点说出密码」，故事才有紧张感。
  • 7–8 → 9+ so it sounded very real → which made the whole thing frighteningly convincing Vocabulary词汇

  • 7–8 → 9+ He kept saying it was urgent. → He kept piling on the pressure Vocabulary词汇
    "Pile on the pressure" is the core idea of this topic's scam texts.pile on the pressure（不断施压）是本主题文章讲骗局时的核心意思。
  • 7–8 → 9+ But something didn't feel right. → What saved her was a nagging feeling that something was off. Listenability好懂程度

  • The 9+ answer uses the cleft "What saved her was ..." to highlight the turning point, weightier than "But".9 级示范用 What saved her was … 的强调句把转折点突出出来，比 But 更有分量。

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 73 words词

Last summer we moved to a new apartment. We paid a moving company. When they put our table down, I saw a big scratch on it.

I took photos. Then I sent an email to the company. At first they did not answer me.

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 110 words词

Last summer we hired a moving company to take our things to our new apartment. When they carried in our dining table, I noticed a long, deep scratch across the top.

I took photos right away, and I asked the movers to write it on the delivery form. Then I emailed the company with the photos. At first they ignored me for two weeks.

So I wrote again, more formally. I listed the date, the damage and the repair quote, and I said I would take it to small claims court if necessary. Three days later, they agreed to pay for the repair.

The lesson? Keep a record of everything.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Verb + -ing or to: the common verbsPast simple and past continuous in storiesVerb and noun endings you cannot skipNumbers, dates, prices and quantitiesReporting verbs with attitude

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 129 words词

Last summer we hired movers for the move to our new apartment, and when they carried in our dining table, I spotted a long, deep scratch right across the top.

I photographed it on the spot and, crucially, had the crew note the damage on the delivery form before they left. Then I emailed the company with the photos attached, only to be ignored for two weeks.

So I followed up with a formal demand letter setting out the date, the damage and a repair quote, and I mentioned, politely but firmly, that small claims court was an option. Within three days they agreed to cover the repair.

What it taught me is that a dispute is usually won by whoever kept the better records, not whoever shouts loudest.

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I took photos. → I took photos right away, and I asked the movers to write it on the delivery form Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Getting the movers to note it on the form is the key step in a claim; saying so makes the content solid.让工人在单据上注明，是维权的关键一步，说出来内容就扎实了。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 At first they did not answer me. → At first they ignored me for two weeks. Vocabulary词汇
    "Ignored" plus a time is more specific than "did not answer".ignore 加上时间，比 did not answer 更具体。
  • 7–8 → 9+ So I wrote again, more formally. → So I followed up with a formal demand letter Vocabulary词汇
    "Demand letter" is a chunk from this topic and names the formal step.demand letter（索赔函）是本主题文章的词块，说出了正式维权的具体做法。
  • 7–8 → 9+ Then I emailed the company with the photos. At first they ignored me for two weeks. → only to be ignored for two weeks Listenability好懂程度
    "Only to ..." joins two sentences and means "but then", which tightens the rhythm.only to … 把两句并成一句，表示「结果却……」，节奏更紧。
  • 7–8 → 9+ The lesson? Keep a record of everything. → a dispute is usually won by whoever kept the better records Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "Dispute" is a chunk from this topic; the lesson becomes a principle you can follow.dispute 是本主题文章的词块；把教训说成一条可以照做的原则。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • The steps in the story (photos on the spot, a note on the delivery form, a formal letter) are what this topic's texts teach, so the content is solid.故事里的维权步骤（当场拍照、让工人在单据上注明、正式去信）就是本主题文章教的做法，讲出来内容就扎实。
  • Dispute, demand letter and deal with are chunks from this topic; "only to be ignored" in the 9+ answer links the email and the silence in one tight sentence.dispute、demand letter、deal with 是本主题文章里的词块；9 级示范 only to be ignored 一句把「去信」和「被无视」连在一起，节奏更紧。
  • The lesson at the end is not empty: it is a principle you can act on (better records win).结尾的教训不是空话，而是一个可以照做的原则（谁记录好谁赢）。

Prompt题目 16 Science stories科学故事

Talk about a time when you changed your mind about something because of new information. 讲一次你因为新信息而改变看法的经历。

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. I believed cracking knuckles caused arthritis我以为掰指关节会得关节炎
  2. I read about a doctor who tested it on himself读到一位医生拿自己做实验
  3. Now I check the evidence before I believe a rule现在先看证据再信
Chunks from the same topic you could use可以用上的同主题词块
  • notice /ˈnəʊtɪs/ 注意到；察觉到
    In the early 1980s, two researchers in Australia noticed something odd. The Doctor Who Drank the Evidence
  • data /ˈdeɪtə/ 数据；资料
    Mine was a mess of mistakes, and my mistakes were data too. The Experiment That Went Wrong
  • change your mind /tʃeɪndʒ jə maɪnd/ 改变主意
    It still took more than ten years, and other teams had to replicate their results in much larger studies, before the medical world changed its mind. The Doctor Who Drank the Evidence
  • hold up /həʊld ʌp/ 经得起检验，站得住脚
    The lab spent the next year following up on it, and the effect held up, but it was much smaller than we had hoped. The Experiment That Went Wrong
  • laugh at /lɑːf æt/ 嘲笑
    The consensus at the time was that no bacterium could survive in stomach acid, so their colleagues were deeply sceptical, and some openly laughed at them. The Doctor Who Drank the Evidence

Three sample answers on the same plan同一骨架的三级示范

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 70 words词

When I was young, my grandmother told me, "Don't crack your fingers. You will get bad joints." I believed her for many years.

Last year I read a story about a doctor. He cracked the fingers on one hand for sixty years, but not the other hand. In the end, both hands were the same.

So I changed my mind. Now I ask for evidence first, before I believe something.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Prepositions of time and place that differ from ChineseScience and discoveryEvaluating: strengths, flaws, trade-offs

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 115 words词

When I was a kid, my grandmother always told me that cracking my knuckles would give me arthritis. I was sure it was true, and I used to tell my own friends the same thing.

Then last year I read about a doctor who tested it on himself. For sixty years, he cracked the knuckles on one hand but not the other. In the end, he found no difference between his two hands.

That changed my mind, but it also taught me something bigger. A lot of things we believe are just repeated, not tested. Now, when I hear a rule like that, I ask, "What's the evidence?" It's a simple habit, but it helps.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： Compound nouns and possessives: a car key, the car's ownerPrepositions of time and place that differ from ChineseNear-synonyms: say, tell, speak, talk and othersScience and discoveryEvaluating: strengths, flaws, trade-offs

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 128 words词

Growing up, my grandmother insisted that cracking my knuckles would give me arthritis, and I took it as gospel. I even passed the warning on to my friends at school, quite proudly.

Then last year I came across the story of a doctor who decided to put it to the test on himself. For sixty years he cracked the knuckles of one hand and left the other alone, and in the end he found no difference whatsoever.

What struck me wasn't just that my grandmother was wrong. It was how many of my beliefs had simply been repeated to me rather than tested. These days, whenever I hear a confident rule like that, my first question is, "What's the evidence?" And quite often, nobody actually knows the answer.

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I believed her for many years. → I was sure it was true, and I used to tell my own friends the same thing. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Adding that you told friends shows how firmly you believed it, so the change matters more.加上「我还告诉朋友」，说明当时信得有多深，后面的转变才有分量。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 In the end, both hands were the same. → In the end, he found no difference between his two hands. Vocabulary词汇
    "Found no difference" is how you report an experiment's result.found no difference 是讲实验结果的说法。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 So I changed my mind. → That changed my mind, but it also taught me something bigger. Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    "Change your mind" is a chunk from this topic; the second half promises a bigger lesson and leads to the ending.change your mind 是本主题文章的词块；后半句预告了更大的收获，引出结尾。
  • 7–8 → 9+ I was sure it was true → I took it as gospel Vocabulary词汇
    "Take something as gospel" is the natural idiom for believing without question.take something as gospel（深信不疑）是地道习语。
  • 7–8 → 9+ a doctor who tested it on himself → a doctor who decided to put it to the test on himself Vocabulary词汇
    "Put it to the test" is the set phrase for testing an idea.put it to the test 是「拿来检验」的固定说法。
  • 7–8 → 9+ A lot of things we believe are just repeated, not tested. → how many of my beliefs had simply been repeated to me rather than tested Listenability好懂程度
    The "how many ..." structure with "rather than" sounds more reflective than the plain sentence.how many … 的感叹结构加 rather than 对比，比原句更有反思味道。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • A changed-my-mind story needs three things: what you believed, what evidence changed it, and what you do now.「改变看法」的经历要讲清三件事：原来信什么、什么证据让你改、改了之后怎么做。
  • The story echoes the self-experiment stories in this topic; change your mind and evidence are chunks from the texts.故事化用了本主题文章里「拿自己做实验」的科学故事，change your mind、evidence 都是文章里的词块。
  • The ending rises from one small fact to a habit (ask for the evidence), which gives Task 2 its "what it meant to you".结尾从一件小事上升到一个习惯（先问证据），Task 2 的「这件事对你的意义」就出来了。

Last year my grandmother, now eighty, moved in with us, and she soon grew isolated because she desperately missed her friends back home. Determined to help, I offered to teach her how to use a smartphone so that she could keep in touch. The early lessons were trying, as she kept tapping the wrong icons and losing heart. What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 After one month she could make video calls → Within a month she was confidently making video calls Vocabulary词汇
    The Level 7 version replaces a plain, vague statement with a more precise one. Adding an adverb and a time expression makes the progress feel concrete and natural.7 分版本把平淡、笼统的说法换成了更精确的表达，加入副词和时间状语，让进步显得具体而自然。
  • 7–8 → 9+ older people can learn new skills → age is no barrier to picking up unfamiliar technology Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    The Level 9 version turns a simple generalisation about older people into a sharper, more reflective point, which gives the story a stronger and more mature conclusion.9 分版本把关于老年人的简单概括升华为更精准、更有思考深度的观点，使故事的结尾更有力、更成熟。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 She is much happier → her mood has improved dramatically Listenability好懂程度
    The Level 8 version replaces a short, flat sentence with a smoother and more descriptive one. This makes the speech sound more natural and easier to follow.8 分版本用更流畅、更有描述性的句子取代了简短平淡的句子，让口语听起来更自然、更容易跟上。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • In Chinese, people often say a plain word for old people. In English, the elderly or older people sounds more respectful and natural than old people, so prefer them in a speaking test.中文里常说「老年人」或「老人家」，英语中 the elderly、older people 或 senior citizens 比 old people 更礼貌、更自然，口语考试里建议优先使用前两者。
  • Use the past tense for the story itself, but switch back to the present tense for a general lesson, as in the sentence about what you learned. This sounds more natural.讲个人经历要用过去时态，但最后的感悟可以转回一般现在时，比如 I learned that... 后面接的常识性结论用现在时，这样听起来更地道。

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 The rent was very high → the rents turned out to be much higher than I had expected Vocabulary词汇
    The upgrade turns a plain statement into a clause that contrasts reality with expectation. ‘Turned out to be much higher than I had expected’ gives the listener more detail and sounds more natural than ‘very high’.升级后的说法把“现实”和“预期”形成对比，信息更丰富，也比简单的 very high 更自然。
  • 7–8 → 9+ the room was cheap, so I managed to save a little money → the bargain rent allowed me to set aside a little money every month Vocabulary词汇
    ‘The bargain rent allowed me to set aside a little money’ uses more precise, idiomatic wording. ‘Set aside’ is a natural phrase for putting money away, and ‘bargain rent’ names the reason directly instead of repeating ‘cheap’ and ‘save’.更高分的说法用词更精准、更地道：set aside 是“存下一点钱”的自然搭配，bargain rent 直接点明原因，避免重复 cheap 和 save。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 The trip to work was very long every day → My daily commute was so long that I often arrived at work exhausted Listenability好懂程度
    The ‘so long that I often arrived at work exhausted’ structure joins cause and result in one smooth sentence. This is easier for a listener to follow than two short, separate sentences.so...that... 结构把原因和结果放进同一个流畅的句子里，听的人比听两个短句更容易跟上。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • Commute works as both a noun and a verb: ‘a long commute’ names the daily trip, while ‘I commute to work’ describes doing it. Saying ‘the way to work is long’ sounds unnatural; ‘my commute is long’ is better.commute 既可以作名词也可以作动词：'a long commute' 指漫长的通勤，'I commute to work' 表示通勤。口语里不要说 ‘the way to work is long’，说 ‘my commute is long’ 更自然。
  • ‘Relocate’ is more formal than ‘move’ and is often used for job-related moves. ‘Settle for’ means accepting a lesser option, which suits stories about housing trade-offs.relocate 比 move 更正式，常用于因工作搬家；settle for 表示退而求其次接受较差的选择，很适合讲住房取舍的故事。

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 82 words词

Last year I decided to stop using so much plastic. I used to buy bottled water every day, and it was bad for the earth. My friend told me about a reusable bottle, so I bought one. At first it was hard because I forgot it often. But after a few weeks I felt happy and I saved money too. Now I also bring my own bags to the store. I think small changes are important, and I want to keep going.

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 117 words词

Last year I decided to cut back on plastic because I was tired of throwing away so many bottles. I used to buy bottled water every day, and I knew it was adding to the pollution that harms our oceans. A friend told me about a reusable bottle, so I bought one the same weekend. At first it was difficult because I kept forgetting it, but I put a reminder on my phone. Within a few weeks it became second nature, and I felt proud of myself. I was also saving money. Now I carry my own bags to the store as well. I believe small changes really matter, and I plan to keep improving my habits.

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 132 words词

Last year I resolved to cut back on plastic, mainly because I was fed up with watching so many bottles pile up in the recycling bin. I used to buy bottled water every single day, and I knew it was adding to the pollution that harms our oceans. A friend introduced me to a reusable bottle, so I bought one that very weekend. The transition was bumpy at first, since I kept leaving the bottle behind, but a simple phone reminder solved that. Within a few weeks it became second nature, and I felt genuinely proud of myself. As a bonus, I was saving money. These days I carry my own bags to the store as well. I truly believe small changes add up, and I intend to keep refining my habits.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 it was bad for the earth → I knew it was adding to the pollution that harms our oceans Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    The upgrade gives a concrete reason, pollution harming the oceans, instead of a vague statement that something is bad for the earth. Specific content makes the story more convincing.升级后的句子给出了具体原因（污染伤害海洋），而不是笼统地说对地球不好。具体的内容让故事更有说服力。
  • 7–8 → 9+ At first it was difficult because I kept forgetting it → The transition was bumpy at first, since I kept leaving the bottle behind Vocabulary词汇
    The Level 9 version describes the difficulty with more precise and idiomatic wording and adds the cause, which makes the sentence sound more natural and varied.9级版本用更精准、更地道的措辞描述困难，并补充了原因，句子听起来更自然、更有变化。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 after a few weeks I felt happy → Within a few weeks it became second nature, and I felt proud of myself Listenability好懂程度
    The upgrade replaces a simple feeling word with a natural expression and a clear result. This is easier to follow and shows the listener a real change over time.升级后用自然的表达和清晰的结果取代了简单的情绪词，听者更容易理解，也能看出随时间发生的真实变化。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • Learners often say ‘protect the environment’ directly. That is correct, but a story is stronger with a specific action such as ‘cut back on plastic’. Concrete verb phrases make the answer more vivid.中文学习者常把环境保护直接说成 protect the environment，这没错，但可以用更具体的动作来讲故事，比如 cut back on plastic（减少塑料）。具体的动词短语能让回答更有画面感。
  • When telling a personal story, use the past tense for events and the present tense for your situation now, as in ‘I used to buy...’ and ‘Now I carry...’. Remember that ‘used to’ is followed by the base form of the verb.讲个人经历时，要用过去时讲故事，用现在时说明现在的状态，例如 I used to buy... 和 Now I carry...。注意 used to 后面接动词原形。

Prompt题目 20 Neighbours and community邻里与社区

Talk about a time when a neighbour helped you with a problem. What happened, and how did it change your relationship with that person? 请讲一讲邻居在你遇到困难时帮助你的一次经历。发生了什么？这件事如何改变了你和这位邻居的关系？

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. Set the scene: a heavy snowstorm and a car stuck in front of my building交代背景：一场大雪，我的车被困在楼前
  2. Explain how the neighbour noticed and helped me dig the car out说明邻居如何发现并帮我把车铲出来
  3. Describe how I thanked him and how our friendship grew afterwards描述我如何感谢他，以及之后我们的友谊如何发展
Chunks from the same topic you could use可以用上的同主题词块
  • branch /brɑːntʃ/ 树枝
    The morning after the windstorm, half the street was outside in rubber boots, looking at branches. The Morning After the Windstorm
  • look /lʊk/ 看起来，显得
    The morning after the windstorm, half the street was outside in rubber boots, looking at branches. The Morning After the Windstorm
  • resident /ˈrezɪdənt/ 居民
    Residents are being asked which services matter most to them, and an online survey will be running until the end of February. Library Branch to Close for Two Years
  • volunteer /ˌvɒlənˈtɪə/ 做义工；义工
    "Every project like this is supposed to finish on time," said one long-time volunteer, who asked not to be named. Library Branch to Close for Two Years
  • neighbourhood /ˈneɪbəhʊd/ 街区；社区；居住区域
    By then, the building will have been serving the neighbourhood for almost sixty years. Library Branch to Close for Two Years

CELPIP 5–6 · ≈B1 84 words词

Last winter, there was a big snowstorm in my town. My car was stuck in the snow and I could not move it. I was very worried because I had to go to work. My neighbour saw me from his window. He came out and helped me. He had a shovel and we worked together for twenty minutes. I was very happy and said thank you many times. Later I made some cookies for him. Now we are good friends and we talk often.

CELPIP 7–8 · ≈B2 113 words词

Last winter, a heavy snowstorm hit my town, and my car got buried in the snow. I was anxious because I had an important meeting at work that morning. I was so grateful that I kept thanking him, even though he insisted it was nothing. A few days later, I baked cookies and knocked on his door to return the favour. Since then, we have become good friends, and we often chat about our street and look out for each other.

CELPIP 9+ · ≈C1 128 words词

Last winter, a ferocious snowstorm hit my town, and overnight my car was buried up to the windows. I was anxious because I had an important meeting that very morning. Fortunately, my neighbour, Mr. Lee, spotted me struggling from his window. Without a second thought, he grabbed his shovel and came out to dig me completely free, and we worked shoulder to shoulder for about twenty minutes. I was so grateful that I could not thank him enough, although he brushed it off as nothing. A few days later, I baked a batch of cookies and knocked on his door to return the favour. Since then, we have struck up a genuine friendship, and we regularly chat over the fence and keep an eye on each other’s homes.

Points from this site used here:这一栏用到的本站知识点： One linker per sentence: although, because, soCountable and uncountable nounsGradable and extreme adjectives: very tired, absolutely exhaustedso, such, too, enough and result clausesLinkers without doublingPrepositions of time and place that differ from ChineseIdioms people actually use

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 He came out and helped me → He grabbed his shovel and came out to dig me free Vocabulary词汇
    The upgrade replaces a vague, basic verb phrase with a vivid, specific action. It shows exactly what the neighbour did and makes the story easier to picture.升级后用具体生动的动作代替了笼统的基础动词短语，清楚说明邻居做了什么，让故事更有画面感。
  • 7–8 → 9+ become good friends → struck up a genuine friendship Listenability好懂程度
    The upgrade swaps a very common phrase for a more natural, idiomatic one that sounds like real spoken English and gives the ending a warmer tone.升级后用更地道、更自然的口语表达代替了常见的简单说法，结尾更有温度，听起来更像真实的英语口语。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was very happy and said thank you many times → I was so grateful that I kept thanking him, even though he insisted it was nothing Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    The upgrade adds a small detail and a reaction from the neighbour, so the thanks feels real and the content is richer and more convincing.升级后加入了邻居的反应这一小细节，让道谢的场景更真实，内容更丰富、更有说服力。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • In Chinese, a common way to say someone helped a lot is translated word for word by learners into an unnatural phrase. A more natural way is to say he was a huge help, or that I could not have managed without him.中文里常说“帮了我很大的忙”，学习者容易逐字翻译成 helped me a big busy。更自然的说法是 he was a huge help 或 I could not have managed without him。
  • When telling a story about the past, keep the verb tenses consistent: use past forms such as was, noticed and grabbed, and switch to the present perfect or present only when you talk about the relationship today.讲过去的故事时，要保持动词时态一致：用 was、noticed、grabbed 这类过去式，只在说现在的关系时才改用 have become 或 are。

Prompt题目 21 Complaints and consumer rights投诉与消费者权益

Talk about a time when you had to complain about a product or a service. What went wrong, what did you do about it, and how did it end? 谈谈你有一次不得不对某件商品或某项服务提出投诉的经历。出了什么问题，你是怎么处理的，最后结果如何？

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. Describe what you bought and what went wrong with it描述你买了什么，以及它出了什么问题
  2. Explain the steps you took to complain, such as emailing and calling说明你投诉时采取的步骤，比如发邮件和打电话
  3. Say how the problem was solved and what you learned说明问题如何解决，以及你学到了什么
Chunks from the same topic you could use可以用上的同主题词块
  • date /deɪt/ 日期；日子

  • keep a record /kiːp ə ˈrekɔːd/ 做记录；留底
    I have kept a record of every call, with dates and the names of the staff I spoke to. A Sofa That Never Arrived
  • refund /ˈriːfʌnd/ (n.), /rɪˈfʌnd/ (v.) 退款
    Our return window is fourteen days, so I can't give you a refund, I'm afraid." "I understand. Not a Return, a Defect
  • a review /ə rɪˈvjuː/ 评论；书评；影评；乐评
    If your goal were only to punish him, a review would do it. Our Bathroom Is Half Finished
  • at least /ət ˈliːst/ 至少；不少于
    I would also ask you to consider some compensation for the two days of work I have lost, or at least an apology from someone who can explain what went wrong. A Sofa That Never Arrived

Last year I splurged on a high-end coffee machine online, only for it to pack up after a single week. I was bitterly disappointed and a little embarrassed, particularly because I had been saving for it for months. I combed through the instruction manual, but there was nothing in it that helped, however hard I tried. green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 paper that came in the box → instruction manual Vocabulary词汇
    The name of the exact document, the instruction manual, is more precise than a vague description of a paper in the box. Precise nouns make the story easier to picture and show a wider vocabulary.用准确的名词 instruction manual（说明书）代替含糊的 paper that came in the box，画面更清晰，也体现更丰富的词汇量。
  • 7–8 → 9+ That experience taught me to stand up for myself → The whole episode taught me that it pays to speak up Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    The lesson is now framed as a general truth that applies beyond this one event, which gives the ending more weight. Linking the lesson to the whole episode also makes the story feel complete.结尾把教训表述成一条普遍适用的道理，并与整个经历相呼应，让故事更完整、更有分量。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 They did not answer for three days → Their silence dragged on for three days Listenability好懂程度
    A vivid phrase about the silence continuing for days replaces a plain negative sentence. It is smoother to listen to and shows the waiting more clearly, with the subject built into one flowing expression.用生动的说法描述对方一连几天没有回音，取代平淡的否定句，听起来更流畅，也更能表现等待的感受。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • Learners often translate the Chinese phrase for ‘returning money’ word by word. In English it is more natural to say ‘get a refund’ or ‘ask for a refund’. ‘Refund’ can be a noun or a verb, so avoid saying ‘return money back’.中文里常说「退钱」，但英语里更自然的说法是 get a refund 或 ask for a refund。refund 既是名词也是动词，不要说成 return money back。
  • When you tell a personal story, give the background first and then move forward in time order with linking words such as ‘first’, ‘then’ and ‘so’. Listeners can follow more easily, and the Listenability score improves.讲个人经历时，先交代背景，再按时间顺序用 first、then、so 等连接词推进，听者更容易跟上，听力评分（Listenability）也更高。

Prompt题目 22 Culture shock and belonging文化冲击与归属

Talk about a time when you felt out of place in a new environment and later began to feel that you belonged. What happened, and what changed for you? 请讲一讲你在新环境中感到格格不入、后来逐渐产生归属感的一次经历。发生了什么？你有什么变化？

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. Describe the new place and why you felt like an outsider at first描述新环境，以及你起初为什么觉得自己是局外人
  2. Explain the moment or event that started to change things说明开始改变局面的那个时刻或事件
  3. Say how you feel now and what you learned about belonging说说你现在的感受，以及你对归属感的体会
Chunks from the same topic you could use可以用上的同主题词块
  • feel /fiːl/ 感觉；摸起来；感到
    "Rarely does a night shift feel like a family, but this one did. Twenty-Two Years of Night Shifts
  • because /bɪˈkɒz/ 因为（引出原因，后面不能再接 so）
    "It is," Lin said, and then, because that felt too short, "I walked from the station." "Did you? Small Talk in the Staff Kitchen
  • feel like /fiːl laɪk/ 想要（做）；感觉像
    "Rarely does a night shift feel like a family, but this one did. Twenty-Two Years of Night Shifts
  • in the room /ɪn ðə ruːm/ 在房间里面
    By Friday she had noticed something: most of the talk in that small room was not made of real questions at all, but of little checks and echoes. Small Talk in the Staff Kitchen
  • left behind /left bɪˈhaɪnd/ 被落下的
    I also feel left behind, as if they have joined a club I cannot join. My Children Feel at Home and I Do Not

I’d like to share what happened during my first month after relocating to a new city for work. Frankly, nothing felt familiar, and since I could not follow the local humour, I felt like a complete outsider. People spoke so quickly that I usually just smiled and stayed silent. I felt deeply isolated, and I even wondered whether I should go back home. Then, one evening, my neighbour invited me over for dinner. Something shifted that night, and I slowly began to feel at ease. Nowadays I have a close circle of friends, and this city has finally become a place I can call home.

green绿色 = new compared with the level below＝比下一级新加的说法 · dashed虚线 = what the next level replaces＝下一级要换掉的说法 · underlined下划线 = a point taught on this site (tap to open it)＝本站教过的知识点（点开去学）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I did not understand the jokes → I could not follow the local humour Vocabulary词汇
    The upgrade replaces a plain verb with a more natural collocation and names the real problem, local humour, so the listener understands exactly what made the speaker feel left out.升级后的说法用了更自然的搭配，并点明真正的困难是听不懂当地的幽默，让听者更清楚是什么让说话者感到被排斥。
  • 7–8 → 9+ From that night on, I felt much more comfortable → Something shifted that night, and I slowly began to feel at ease Listenability好懂程度
    The upgrade turns a flat statement of feeling into a short, vivid description of a turning point, with smoother rhythm and an idiomatic expression that sounds more natural when spoken.升级后的说法把平淡的感受陈述变成对转折点的简短生动描述，节奏更顺，用语也更地道，口语听起来更自然。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was nervous but I went → Although I was anxious, I decided to accept Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    The upgrade adds a contrast with a subordinate clause and a clear decision, so the listener hears the speaker’s inner conflict and not only the action.升级后的说法用从句表达对比并写出明确的决定，让听者听到说话者内心的挣扎，而不仅是一个动作。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • In Chinese you might simply say that you were nervous but went anyway. In spoken English, a concession clause with although makes the contrast sound more natural and closer to a high-scoring answer.中文里常说“我很紧张但我去了”，英语口语中用 although 引导让步从句，能让转折更自然，也更接近高分表达。
  • When telling a personal story, keep it in time order: background first, the turning point in the middle, and how you feel now at the end. This is easy for listeners to follow and supports task fulfilment.讲个人经历时，请按时间顺序组织：开头交代背景，中间讲转折，结尾说现在的感受。这样听者容易跟上，也有利于任务完成度。

Prompt题目 23 Driving and getting around开车与出行

Talk about a time when you had trouble getting somewhere on time because of traffic or another travel problem. What happened, how did you handle it, and what did you learn? 请讲述一次你因为堵车或其他出行问题而难以按时到达某地的经历。发生了什么？你是如何处理的？你学到了什么？

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. Set the scene: where you were going and why it was important交代背景：你要去哪里，以及为什么这件事很重要
  2. Describe the travel problem and the steps you took to solve it描述遇到的出行问题以及你采取的解决步骤
  3. Explain the result and the habit you changed afterwards说明结果，以及事后你改变了什么习惯

  • black ice /blæk ˈaɪs/ 黑冰（路面上看不见的薄冰）

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 I left home late → I didn’t leave myself enough time Vocabulary词汇
    The new wording uses a natural expression about managing time and shows that the speaker takes responsibility for the problem, not just that the departure was late.新说法使用了关于时间安排的地道表达，说明说话人认识到问题出在自己身上，而不只是出门晚了。
  • 7–8 → 9+ wasn’t very fast → was hardly a shortcut Vocabulary词汇
    This phrase uses understatement and ties the idea to the detour, which sounds more precise and expressive than a basic comment about speed.这个短语用了含蓄的反说手法，并紧扣“绕路”这一情节，比简单评价速度快慢更精准、更有表现力。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 I was very worried → I started to panic Listenability好懂程度
    Describing the moment the feeling began is more vivid than a general adjective and helps the listener follow how the tension builds.描述情绪开始出现的那一刻，比笼统的形容词更生动，也让听者更容易感受到紧张感的升级。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • Do not translate the Chinese verb meaning ‘meet’ literally when talking about congestion. Say ‘run into a traffic jam’ or ‘hit traffic’ instead.表达“遇上堵车”时，不要把中文的“遇见”直译成 meet a traffic jam，应说 run into a traffic jam 或 hit traffic。
  • Adding ‘pulled over’ before the phone call makes the order of events clear and also shows safe driving habits.故事里加上 pulled over（靠边停车）再打电话，既交代了动作顺序，也体现了安全驾驶意识。

What changes from level to level每升一级换了什么

  • 5–6 → 7–8 The food was very good → Every dish was full of flavour Vocabulary词汇
    The Level 7 wording replaces a vague, repeated adjective with a more specific description of the food, which makes the story more vivid and precise.7 分版本用更具体的描述代替了笼统且重复的形容词，让食物的细节更生动、更准确。
  • 7–8 → 9+ laughing about old family stories → swapping embarrassing childhood anecdotes until our sides ached Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    The Level 9 wording swaps a general statement for a concrete, memorable detail. Specific, lively images make the ending more engaging and natural to listen to.9 分版本用具体而难忘的细节代替了笼统的说法，画面感更强，结尾更吸引人，听起来也更自然。
  • 5–6 → 7–8 we waited a long time → the last dish took nearly forty minutes to arrive Content / Coherence内容与连贯
    Instead of saying only that the wait was long, the improved wording gives a clear detail about how long it was, which supports the point and adds useful content.改进后的说法没有只说等了很久，而是给出了清楚的细节，既支撑了观点，也增加了有效内容。
Notes on this prompt这道题的讲解
  • When describing food in speech, avoid repeating very good. Use more specific phrases such as full of flavour, delicious or mouth-watering to score higher.口语里描述食物时，不要反复使用 very good。可以换成 full of flavour、delicious、mouth-watering 等更具体的表达，评分会更高。
  • When telling a personal story, use The only problem was that... to introduce a small complication. It gives the story shape and leads smoothly into your ending.讲个人经历时，用 The only problem was that... 引出小插曲，能让故事有起伏，也方便你自然地过渡到结尾。

Prompt题目 25 Public health and evidence公共卫生与证据

Talk about a time when you changed your mind about a health claim after you looked at the evidence. What did you hear, how did you check it, and what did you learn from the experience? 请讲一讲你在查看证据后改变了对某个健康说法的看法的一次经历。你听到了什么，是如何核实的，从中学到了什么？

Plan: three points to cover提纲：要讲的三点
  1. Explain the health claim you first believed and who told you.说明你最初相信的健康说法，以及是谁告诉你的。
  2. Describe how you searched for reliable evidence and what you found.描述你如何寻找可靠证据，以及你发现了什么。
  3. Share how the experience changed your habits.分享这次经历如何改变了你的习惯。
Chunks from the same topic you could use可以用上的同主题词块

  • findings /ˈfaɪndɪŋz/ 研究结果；调查结论

  • explain /ɪkˈspleɪn/ 解释；说明
    We therefore changed our approach and allowed participants to explain their experiences in their own words. What Our Community Survey Revealed
  • on the whole /ɒn ðə həʊl/ 总体上；大体而言
    On the whole, community feedback tends to be more valuable when it is interpreted alongside other evidence. What Our Community Survey Revealed
  • also /ˈɔːlsəʊ/ 也；还（通常放在动词前、be 动词后）
